finding_candidates.rationale: Delta versus the packet: FND-0185 gives only the sufficiency direction and remarks informally that non-Tate source summands 'may die in the map to T'; FND-0188 compares that hypothesis with RED-0001; FND-0168(3a) gives necessity from K downwards. None of them records that the interface surjection splits, hence none states the exact criterion, and the splitting is what converts an unusable sufficient condition into a single well-posed question about a canonical subobject of A. Reusable because it applies to every kernel-form term of the FND-0181/FND-0182 nested family, it tells the proof and counterexample lanes that they are computing the same object ker(q) from opposite sides, and it makes precise which non-Tate witnesses (FND-0053, FND-0170, FND-0176) could ever matter. Requires independent corroboration of the isotypic-component step and of polarizability as imported from FND-0185.
finding_candidates.statement: Let Y be a closed substack of X=M_{6,6}, A:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q), T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q), and let q:A->T_Z be the surjection of FND-0180/FND-0168(3a) onto the kernel-form term. By FND-0185, A is a pure polarizable Q-Hodge structure of weight -16, and polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures of fixed weight form a semisimple abelian category (FND-0033). Hence q splits, A is isomorphic to ker(q) direct-sum T_Z, and morphisms preserve canonical isotypic components, so writing A = A_Tate direct-sum A_nonTate for the canonical splitting into the Q(8)-isotypic part and its complement one gets (T_Z)_nonTate = q(A_nonTate). Therefore T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8) if and only if A_nonTate is contained in ker(q). Two lane consequences: a C66-TATE-SUPPORT proof routed through the verified interface source may replace the FND-0185 hypothesis 'A is Tate' by the strictly weaker and canonical 'A_nonTate is contained in ker(q)', and a C66-CEX-LOCAL / C66-CEX-SURVIVE disproof through the same interface must exhibit a non-Tate isotypic summand of A with nonzero image in T, which is the theorem's survival clause in checkable form. Exhibiting a non-Tate class anywhere in A, in an atlas, in a family base, or in a standalone product model settles neither lane.

strongest_attack: Strongest attack, and it succeeds: the artifact never discharges its own theorem_statement, and its target_interface_reference is therefore a correctly-named interface carrying a conditional in place of a proof. ATT-0123 concedes this itself (CLM-0123-3 status 'gap', GAP-0123-1 severity high, resolves_exact_target=false), so the interesting adversarial work is whether anything in it either (i) hides an error that would push to refuted, or (ii) hides an unclaimed advance that would rescue it. Neither holds. On (ii): the artifact's two proved claims are both already adjudicated packet findings. CLM-0123-1 is FND-0180 (with FND-0168(3) and the FND-0185 duality), CLM-0123-2 is FND-0185 verbatim in content ('sufficient, not necessary; non-Tate summands of the source may die in the map to T'). Neither finding is cited anywhere in dependency_claim_ids, proof_dependencies, or source_ids; ATT-0123 instead attributes the Borel-Moore image form to CLM-0120-2..5, which do not state it (CLM-0120-3/4 define T_Z purely as the ordinary-cohomology kernel ker(T->W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6}\Y;Q)(21)), and ATT-0120 section 0 declines standalone theories on the singular closed Y), and to a REV-0169 reasoning note plus an uncorroborated review candidate, which the packet's execution boundary rules out as evidence ('No raw review or candidate finding is evidence in this packet'). That misattribution is a real provenance defect but not a mathematical one, since FND-0180/FND-0185 make the step available. On (i) I ran the full checklist and found no error to exploit. Degrees, weights, twists: 2*21-16=26 and 26-2*21=-16, T is Borel-Moore degree 16 weight -16, Q(8) is Hodge type (-8,-8) of weight -16 (not Q(-8), which is the dual compact-support corner of FND-0168(1)), and ATT-0123 keeps FND-0001's Poincare identification distinct from FND-0168(1)'s duality rather than conflating them. Gysin: none is taken, and the map used, Borel-Moore proper pushforward i_*:H^{BM}_{16}(Y)->H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}), is degree- and twist-preserving, so no shift by twice a codimension and no fundamental class of Y appears; the FND-0052 / FND-0168(5a)/(5b) obligations are routed around, not assumed away, and FND-0147's monomorphism is not upgraded to a closed immersion. Kunneth: no product decomposition is used. Spectral sequences: only a long exact localization sequence, so no differential or degeneration bookkeeping is owed. Stack versus coarse moduli and integral versus rational coefficients: everything is stack-level with Q-coefficients, and no FND-0075/FND-0144 content is engaged. Invariants versus coinvariants under S_6 or graph automorphisms: not engaged, since the ordered model maps to the ordered stack and Y is formed in M_{6,6}; FND-0152(ii) is respected in that no induction/transfer identity is upgraded to Tate type. Semisimplification versus actual isomorphism: CLM-0123-2 is an honest Hodge-structure isomorphism argument on a pure weight -16 object, and FND-0033 removes any extension gap. Predicted motives, and pure Tate upgraded to algebraic or tautological generation: neither appears, and no Hodge-conjecture step of the FND-0168(4) type is taken. Omitted stable pairs: none is omitted because no compactification or boundary accounting is opened at all; the theorem itself excludes assembly of complementary terms, and the one-sided coverage inherited from CLM-0120-5 inflates rather than omits. Second attack, on the disproof clause: the artifact's counterexample audit is correct in refusing FND-0176/FND-0178's (10,6) constant-product witness and any atlas or family-base non-Tateness as a refutation, because the theorem's survival clause demands a non-Tate subquotient of this named T_Z, and FND-0171 records that corner injections do not propagate non-Tateness; so no refutation is available from the artifact's own material either, and refuted is not the correct verdict. Third attack, on the choice of sufficient condition: routing through Tate-ness of A=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) is strictly stronger than the theorem needs, since T_Z is only a quotient of A, and FND-0053, FND-0170 and FND-0176 make it live that A carries non-Tate summands; in the weakest-sufficient-proof lane the artifact thus adopts an antecedent that is both unproved and plausibly false, which is why the conditional cannot be repaired by supplying more of the same interface. theorem_statement: Let T_Z be the canonical mixed-Hodge subquotient of T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) supplied by a verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum. Prove T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8). A disproof must exhibit a non-Tate subquotient of this named T_Z through the verified target interface; non-Tate cohomology of an arbitrary family base, atlas, product model, standalone Z, or a source class whose target image is not proved nonzero is not a disproof. This theorem does not itself assemble the complementary target terms.
